sources.method: CHM catalogue 102730615 prints '8.26w x 2.54h x 9.52l (cm)'; ×10 to mm (82.6, 25.4, 95.2); axes as CHM labels them: w→width, h→height, l→depth.

sources.quote: Atari 2600 Moon Patrol video game cartridge, for use for 2600 machine and joystick.

notes: Computer History Museum catalogue records of three bare cartridges: Moon Patrol (Atari, Inc., 1982, 102730615), Laser Blast (Activision, 1981, 102730617) and California Games (1987, 102730618). All three carry the identical figure '3 1/4w x 1h x 3 3/4l (in)', so CHM's record is a quarter-inch-rounded catalogue envelope, and it does not separate the publishers' different shells (Atari and Activision shells are known to differ in detail). Treat it as an ENVELOPE ONLY, ±1/8 in (±3.2 mm) per axis; a preset needs measured shells per publisher (measurement queue).

Axis order is CHM's own labelling (w, h, l) for the cartridge lying flat: width=82.6 (w), height=25.4 (h, the thickness), depth=95.2 (l, the insertion length). CHM's centimetre line is CHM's own conversion; the millimetre values are a ×10 shift (derived source). The CHM masses (0.5 lb, whole/half pounds) are not used.
edge_contacts, contact_pitch_mm, insertion_edge, shutter (Atari shells have a sliding dust door), card and pass_through_slot: no value-tier source read states them; null.
